title: Encouraging Responsible Use of Generative AI in Education: A Reward-Based Learning Approach
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a growing concern in education: students' use of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT to obtain immediate answers to homework and assignments without engaging in the underlying learning process. The authors argue that direct-answer AI tools may weaken foundational understanding, reduce productive cognitive effort, and undermine structured learning, especially in mathematics. In response, the paper proposes an approach intended to encourage responsible AI use by shifting students away from answer-seeking and toward step-by-step concept development.

The intervention introduced is MEGA (Math Explorer & Guidance Assistant), a multimodal chatbot built on OpenAI's GPT-4o model. Students can submit math problems either as text or images. Rather than directly solving the original problem, MEGA first identifies the problem type, then presents a similar but simpler problem with step-by-step explanation, followed by a related challenge problem. Only after the learner successfully solves the challenge problem does the system reveal the solution to the original question as a reward. The system is framed as a reward-based learning mechanism designed to reinforce concepts, promote engagement, and support responsible AI-assisted study habits.

The paper does not report a human-subjects evaluation with a defined participant sample. Instead, it illustrates the system through example interactions for text-based and image-based math queries and reports performance across 70 math questions spanning categories such as linear equations, quadratic equations, factorials, coordinate geometry, triangle classification, and trigonometry. The context is educational mathematics problem-solving, but no specific grade band, institution, or classroom deployment is described.

The main conclusion is that a generative AI system can be designed to support conceptual reinforcement instead of shortcut answer retrieval. The authors conclude that MEGA's indirect, reward-based approach offers a promising way to foster active engagement and more responsible AI use in education. They also suggest the approach could be extended beyond mathematics and enhanced with gamified features such as badges, points, and leaderboards, though these future directions remain conceptual rather than empirically validated.

identified_tools.name: MEGA
identified_tools.description: Math Explorer & Guidance Assistant (MEGA) is a multimodal LLM-based math chatbot that uses OpenAI GPT-4o to accept text or image math inputs and guide learners through indirect, step-by-step conceptual reinforcement with a reward-based release of the original solution.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper presents MEGA as a math learning assistant that gives students analogous practice problems and only reveals the solution to the original problem after they successfully solve a related challenge problem.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports descriptive accuracy rates for MEGA across 70 math questions by problem category and input type, rather than a comparative learning-outcomes study. Accuracy was higher for text than image input across categories: linear equations 85% vs 65%, quadratic equations 75% vs 60%, coordinate geometry 65% vs 55%, factorial 80% vs 70%, triangle classification by angles 75% vs 67%, and trigonometry 64% vs 60%.
findings.measure: Problem-solving accuracy on 70 math questions by category and input type (text vs image)

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's ChatGPT is a generative AI chatbot based on GPT-family large language models that provides direct responses to user queries.
identified_tools.use_case: ChatGPT is discussed as the contrast condition/problematic baseline that can provide immediate answers to student math questions and potentially bypass structured learning; it is not empirically evaluated in a controlled comparison.

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's Gemini is a generative AI chatbot/LLM assistant for conversational question answering.
identified_tools.use_case: Gemini is mentioned in the introduction as an example of a generative AI tool offering instant responses; it is not directly studied.

quality_tier_rationale: This is primarily a system/prototype paper with illustrative interactions and descriptive accuracy summaries, but no clear experimental evaluation of student outcomes, no control group, and no rigorous study design details.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially useful performance on math problem handling, but impact on learning is unclear because no effect sizes, comparative intervention results, or direct student outcome evidence are reported.
